exemplar.title: What strong work looks like
exemplar.intro: A strong aquarium proposal defends every pane of glass — here is how one student designed a classroom terrarium.

traits.sample: My terrarium is 24 in × 12 in × 16 in, so V = 4,608 cubic inches — enough for two geckos by the care guide.
traits.why: The volume is computed and then checked against a real requirement.

traits.trait: Counts only the glass faces needed
traits.sample: A terrarium has no glass top, so I added five faces, not six: 2(384) + 2(192) + 288 = 1,440 in² of glass.
traits.why: Surface area is adapted to the real build, not just the formula.

traits.sample: Glass costs $0.05 per square inch, so 1,440 × 0.05 = $72 — under my $80 budget with sealant to spare.
traits.why: The cost line follows directly from the surface-area math.

traits.trait: Compares designs by cost per volume
traits.sample: My wide design costs $0.016 per cubic inch of habitat; the tall one costs $0.019 — wide wins.
traits.why: A rate makes two differently-shaped tanks comparable.
